subject: Lakeside: inference response consistency — findings and corrective actions
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lakeside-finance.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Asha Mehra <asha.mehra@lakeside-finance.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jan 2028 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected variation in inference outputs (Lakeside account)

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing a notable change in answer phrasing for our underwriting prompts around 02:45 UTC yesterday. The quality variance is causing downstream rule mismatches — two manual review queues filled up and a few automated tags were missed. Details:
- Sample request ids: req_7a2f, req_7a53 (attached samples).
- Observed: model replies shorter, dropped contextual constraint about risk thresholds.

This looks like an internal Redwood model behavior change on your side. Can you confirm whether a model variant or rollout impacted Lakeside? We need an initial readout and estimated ETA for a fix; our compliance team is waiting.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Risk Operations
Lakeside Finance

Attachments: samples.zip (6 text files)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lakeside-finance.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 06 Jan 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected variation in inference outputs (Lakeside account)

Hi Daniel — thank you for the quick heads up and the sample requests. We escalated immediately to the infra and model-onboarding teams. Preliminary notes:

- No intentional model change was scheduled for Lakeside yesterday.
- We saw a correlated increase in short-lived KV-cache evictions on the serving fleet that coincide with the timestamp you provided.
- We’re treating this as a behavioral impact caused by a service-side regression (KV cache eviction + fallback to smaller context window).

Next steps for the day:
1) We’ll provide a timeline of events and a root cause hypothesis by Monday.
2) If confirmed, we will roll a targeted fix to Lakeside’s routing policy to pin your sessions to the stable cache profile and re-run your sample requests.

I’ll loop in Marissa and Hannah on remediation scheduling and customer communications. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your compliance flows.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Reliability
Redwood Inference

Marissa

On Sat, Jan 06, 2028 at 10:03 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Daniel — thank you for the quick heads up and the sample requests...
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lakeside-finance.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 07:20:00 -0800
Subject: Lakeside RCA and corrective actions (summary + attachments)

Daniel / Asha — thank you for your patience. Attached is the concise RCA and the supporting logs. Executive summary below; full doc is in the attached PDF.

Executive summary:
- Impact window: 2028-01-04T02:40:00Z through 2028-01-04T03:20:00Z (UTC).
- Root cause: a recent serving runtime scheduler change increased transient memory pressure under a particular request shape; this triggered excessive KV-cache evictions on ~3% of serving shards. Eviction caused shortfalls in context available to the model, which manifested as truncated/less-constrained replies for requests relying on prefix caching.
- Customer-visible effect: shorter replies and omitted constraint tokens for a subset of requests; not a model weight or prompt change.

Actions completed (immediate):
1) Rolled targeted routing pin for Lakeside session buckets to the stable cache-profile (completed 2028-01-04T03:35:00Z).
2) Hotfix reverted the scheduler heuristic causing the pressure spike (completed 2028-01-04T04:02:00Z).
3) Replayed the sample request set and verified that responses matched pre-incident baselines (log excerpts attached).

Planned actions (next 30 days):
- Extended automated KV-cache telemetry (alerts + retention) — ETA 2028-01-14.
- Add a short-circuit validation in rollout CI so scheduler heuristic changes run a KV-stability check — ETA 2028-01-20.
- Full post-incident audit and improved canary coverage for the scheduler subsystem — ETA 2028-02-01.

Compensation and SLAs:
- We’ll issue a goodwill credit for the impacted token usage during the window; Marissa is following up on credit amount and paperwork.

Attachments: lakeside_rca.pdf (detailed timeline, logs), kv-eviction-logs.txt (server-side excerpts).

Please let us know if you want a walkthrough call; we have an opening Wednesday 2028-01-11 at 11:00 PT or Thursday 2028-01-12 at 09:00 PT.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll take the learnings to prevent recurrence.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Reliability
Redwood Inference
